transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Argus - Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Argus - Eng Manager), Priya Singh (Argus - Security)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on Redwood PLG/self-serve quickstart, time-to-first-token, free credits, and how Argus might evaluate hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Security and compliance questions surfaced; team requested benchmarks and SOC2 docs. Next steps agreed around quickstart credits and a technical deep-dive/benchmark.

Topics: quickstart flow, credits, API keys, SDKs, sample throughput/latency, dedicated capacity, VPC/private deployments, SOC2/KMS, rollout timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sophie from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. Diego our SE is with me. How are you all?
[00:08] Maya: Good thanks, Maya here. We're excited to hear what Redwood offers, we saw the quickstart page and wanted to understand time to first token and what the free credits look like.
[00:16] Diego: Great, hi Maya, hi Liam, Priya, quick intro
I'll run through the quickstart experience and then we can dig into hosted vs dedicated and security.
[00:26] Liam: Cool. For context, we run a mix of online inference for chat features and batch embeddings for search, currently on a mix of in-house GPUs and managed endpoints; cost is creeping up.
[00:35] Priya: And security is big for us, we need SOC2, SSO via SAML, audit logs, and we use AWS KMS.
[00:44] Sophie: Totally makes sense. The quickstart is PLG/self-serve
sign up, get a free credit bundle, you can create an API key and hit the REST endpoint in minutes. Typically teams see first token within a few minutes of signup.
[00:56] Maya: When you say minutes, is that from sign up or from provisioning a dedicated pool?
[01:01] Diego: For hosted API, it's immediate
time to first token is basically the time to grab an API key and call. If you wantDedicated, there's a small provisioning window depending on GPU type; that can be hours to a day. Our Dedicated product is called Redwood Dedicated
pologies, sometimes the docs call it Dedicated capacity, little naming mix up in our slo, but the idea is reserved capacity.
[01:20] Liam: Ok that matches what we thought. For benchmarks, do you provide sample numbers for latency/throughput for the open models?
[01:26] Diego: Yes, we have performance profiles in the catalog
throughput/latency vary by model, sequence length and batching. We'll send a benchmark template so you can plug in your payloads. Also we recommend prefix caching and batching to lower unit cost.
[01:38] Maya: Do you support streaming responses and function calling?
[01:41] Sophie: Yes, streaming, function/tool calling, structured output supported in the hosted API.
[01:46] Priya: On security, does Redwood Hosted ever persist customer data? What's your retention policy, and can we restrict retention?
[01:53] Diego: Hosted is opt-in for retention; by default ephemeral, but you can opt into longer retention for debugging. For enterprise, we also have Redwood Private and Dedicated where data stays in your VPC or on-prem. We integrate with KMS/HSM for key management, support SSO/SAML and RBAC.
[02:10] Priya: Are audit logs exported to our SIEM?
[02:13] Diego: Yes, we can stream audit logs, or you can pull them via the control plane. We'll include details in the security pack.
[02:20] [00:02:20] Maya: Great. On pricing do you do usage-based for hosted and committed for dedicated?
[02:27] Sophie: Exactly. Hosted is per-token (and per-embedding unit), Dedicated is reserved commits with burst options. We can work up a committed estimate if you give rough QPS and token per request.
[02:37] Liam: For our use case, average request is 512 tokens, around 100 qps at peak for chat, and 200 concurrent batch embedding jobs overnight.
[02:48] Diego: That helps. For 512 tokens at 100 QPS you'd want to consider Dedicated for predictability; but for initial evaluation PLG hosted with quickstart credits is usually fastest. You can run a pilot on hosted to validate accuracy/latency and then move to Dedicated when you need SLAs.
[03:04] Maya: What's involved in moving from hosted to Private? Is it a big migration?
[03:08] Diego: The API surface is the same
same endpoints and SDKs
so client changes are minimal. The difference is vpn/vpc networking, control plane access, and we help with infra setup for Private. We have a deployment checklist we'll share.
[03:20] Priya: About compliance do you have SOC2 and ISO?
[03:23] Sophie: We are SOC2 Type II and have an ISO roadmap; we'll send the attestation and the security pack.
[03:29] Maya: Will you give us sample cURL/SDK snippets? We want to try generating with our prompt templates.
[03:34] Sophie: Absolutely, we include quickstart snippets for cURL, python and node
I'll send those and a sample postman collection.
[03:40] [00:03:40] Liam: Any gotchas around rate limits when using free credits?
[03:44] Diego: Free credits come with soft rate limits to prevent abuse but are generous enough for evaluation. If you need higher QPS for benchmarking we'll coordinate to lift them temporarily.
[03:52] Maya: What about model versions and rollouts an we pin models?
[03:56] Sophie: Yes, you can pin model versions and configure rollout policies, canary, A/B tests, automatic fallback. The Console shows per-model metrics.
[04:04] Priya: Do you cache requests or prefix cache and how does that interact with PII?
[04:08] Diego: Caching is optional, and you control what is cached. For PII we recommend disabling prefix caching or using dedicated private deployments where caching can be constrained.
[04:18] Maya: For the quickstart pilot, what's the typical timeline?
[04:21] Sophie: Sign up and first token in minutes, run initial eval over 1-2 days, then a 1-2 week pilot for more realistic traffic.
[04:28] Maya: Sounds good. Could you also share any cost optimization tips?
[04:31] Diego: Sure
use quantized model variants for lower cost, tune batching, enable prefix/KV caching where appropriate, and pick models with a good cost/quality tradeoff. We can recommend quantization settings based on your workload.
[04:43] Liam: How does Redwood compare to Bedrock or Anthropic operationally?
[04:46] Sophie: Many customers choose Redwood for production-first inference controls, unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, and tight observability. If you need full managed endpoints with no infra work, Bedrock is similar, but Redwood focuses on inference economics and rollout controls which helps at scale.
[04:59] Maya: Ok next steps from our side: Priya will compile a compliance list, Liam will share traffic profile and prompts, and Maya will run a quick pilot with Redwood quickstart credits.
[05:10] Sophie: I'll follow up with the credit link, quickstart doc, SOC2 and the benchmark template. Diego will follow up on the technical deep dive.
[05:16] [00:05:16] Priya: One question do you support private deployment on-prem for air-gapped environments?
[05:20] Diego: Yes, we offer Private (VPC and on-prem options) for regulated customers. On-prem requires more lead time and we provide an installer and integration docs.
[05:29] Maya: For our evaluation, we'll start hosted and evaluate migration to Dedicated or Private depending on latency and security.
[05:34] Sophie: Perfect. Anything else?
[05:36] Liam: Not from me.
[05:38] Maya: No.
[05:39] Sophie: Ok thanks everyone, we'll send the materials and get the deep-dive on the calendar.

End of transcript.
